```{python}
#| label: setup
import sys, os
from pathlib import Path

# Resolve the compartment root by walking up to the sentinel config, then put 02_analysis on
# the path so `from helpers...` works whether this is opened from the notebook dir or the root.
# The `d.parent == d` guard is load-bearing: at "/" the parent is "/" again, so without it a
# missing sentinel spins forever instead of telling you what is wrong.
SENTINEL = "02_analysis/config/analysis_config.yaml"
START = Path.cwd().resolve()
d = START
while not (d / SENTINEL).exists():
    if d.parent == d:
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"compartment root ({SENTINEL}) not found above {START}\n"
            "  -> open the explorer from inside the compartment tree.")
    d = d.parent
os.chdir(d)
sys.path.insert(0, str(d / "02_analysis"))

# Imports go through the per-project shim 02_analysis/helpers/interactive_style.py (scaffolded
# in the project); it re-exports the contract lib symlinked at
# 02_analysis/helpers/interactive-style/ — a hyphenated dir is not an importable package.
from helpers.interactive_style import (
    load_interactive_config, load_explorer, grid, close_panels,
    first_selection, save_selection, snapshot)
import jscatter  # noqa: F401  (the live widget backend)

config = load_interactive_config()
df = load_explorer("[NN]_[stage]", config=config)   # <- compact parquet name (no _explore suffix)
print(df.shape, "cells")
df.head(3)
```

## Color by an annotation

Edit `CHANNELS` and re-run the grid to recolor. `cat=` forces categorical (else inferred by
dtype); `interactive.categorical_obs` in config is always categorical.

```{python}
#| label: grid
CHANNELS = ["[gene_or_score]", "[qc_metric]", "[label]", "[batch_or_tissue]"]

PANELS = grid(df, CHANNELS)   # grid() closes any prior panels FIRST — OOM-safe, never a raw loop
PANELS
```

Four linked panels — brush or lasso any one, the rest highlight the same cells. Look for the
pocket you want to characterize, then run the next cell.

```{python}
#| label: close-escape-hatch
# ESCAPE HATCH — run this standalone if a grid ever lags. grid() calls it for you on every
# re-run; this is here for the manual case (ipywidgets keep every panel alive until closed).
close_panels()
```

## Characterize the selection

```{python}
#| label: characterize
import pandas as pd
sel = first_selection()          # reads the LIVE panels grid() registered — no variable traps
sub = df.iloc[sel]
if len(sub) == 0:
    print("Brush or lasso a cluster in the grid above, then re-run.")
else:
    cols = [c for c in CHANNELS if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(df[c])]
    print(f"{len(sub)} cells selected")
    display(pd.DataFrame({"selected": sub[cols].mean(),
                          "all": df[cols].mean()}).round(3))
```

**What we see.**
<!-- the reading that informs the call — what IS this pocket -->

## Save — barcodes + a labelled snapshot

jscatter's own export grabs only the points (no legend/axes). `save_selection` writes the
barcodes (re-loadable later); `snapshot` writes a labelled figure. Both land under the
notebook's `eda/`.

```{python}
#| label: save
LABEL = "[name_the_pocket]"                       # <- name it
sel = first_selection()
save_selection(df, sel, label=LABEL, subdir="[NN]_[stage]_explore", config=config)
snapshot(df, "[gene_or_score]", name=LABEL, subdir="[NN]_[stage]_explore",
         indices=sel, config=config)
```

```{python}
#| label: reload
# Barcodes are the durable currency — re-derive indices in a later session from the saved CSV.
saved = pd.read_csv(f"02_analysis/notebooks/[NN]_[stage]_explore/eda/selection_{LABEL}.csv",
                    index_col=0)
sel_reloaded = df.index.get_indexer(saved.index)
sel_reloaded = sel_reloaded[sel_reloaded >= 0]
print(f"reloaded {len(sel_reloaded)} of {len(saved)} barcodes")
```
